text:
**Short answer: the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is the pick if you want a day or more of heat.** It's a small, steady load, so a portable power station suits it well.

**Why this one**
- According to [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage), the Elite 200 V2 has 2,073.6 Wh (LiFePO4) and a 2,600 W output. That should run a 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat for about a day. It's listed at $899 and in stock, and the page says the code DEALECTRIC saves $44.95. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). Dealectric is a retailer, so this is a sales page.
- Reptile heat doesn't need much power. The same source lists under-tank heat mats at 4–24 W, ceramic emitters at 50–150 W and deep heat projectors at 50–80 W. A thermostat only runs them part of the time.
- A power station usually beats a small battery backup here. [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says you need sustained watts for hours, not just a clean handoff. Its runtimes are arithmetic (Wh ÷ watts), not tests, so real results will vary.

**Other options from the same source ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))**
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, $449): about 15–18 hours for a 100 W emitter on a thermostat. It's back in stock in late November.
- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh, $289.99): about 6–8 hours for a 24 W heat mat. This is enough for a short outage and a small enclosure.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3** (1,024 Wh): the page doesn't list a price, and it sends you to Amazon for price and stock.

**Tips**
- A heat mat lasts much longer than a lamp on the same battery. Insulate the enclosure first, since that stretches your runtime ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage)). A Reddit keeper wrapped terrariums in insulation ([r/reptiles](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/)).
- Add a cheap backup, such as chemical hand warmers or wrapped warm water bottles ([Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage)).
- Most healthy adult reptiles can tolerate roughly 24–48 hours of a temperature drop. Hatchlings, sick animals and tropical species like chameleons are more vulnerable ([Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pets-reptiles-during-a-power-outage)). Check with your vet about your species.
- Don't feed your reptile until it's warm again ([Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage)).

Check your heater's actual wattage and divide the station's Wh by it, with some margin, before you buy.
